criteria.evidence: Measured over HTTP against the production build, not asserted: GET / returns 307 with location: /login. routes/index.spec.ts drives the exported redirigirALogin and asserts isRedirect plus headers.get('Location') === '/login' — the one thing no compiler watches, since href is a bare string.

The two of the six this step owes: the / redirect (307) and the * 404. The other four arrive with Groups 9–12; /login, /register, /invite/abc123 and /profile all return 200 today rendering the designed 404 inside the shell, which is §3's declared pattern for a forward link, not a failure.

No route in the diff checks a session, permission or token: _app.tsx has only a loader calling the shell repository, _app/$.tsx has no loader, index.tsx has only beforeLoad throwing the redirect. Every URL probed (/profile, /circles, /uploads, /help, /privacy, /nope/deep/path) opens directly with 200 and no redirect.

No form exists in this step's surface, and nothing in estado.ts validates input in the rejecting sense: parseEstado narrows or returns undefined, never throws and never redirects. The designed error states are visitable scenarios by construction.

The 404 is a splat route child of the pathless layout rather than the router's defaultNotFoundComponent, which is what puts it inside the shell and keeps the unmatched URL in the address bar. Measured: /nope/deep/path returns 200, the rendered page carries the shell navigation at both widths (bottom-nav visible at 390x844, side-nav 264px at 1230), and the URL is unchanged.

apps/web/src/components/ is absent from the tree (home-page.tsx and its spec were removed at c40033a in step 3); this step delivers the second half — routes/index.tsx now has no component of its own, only beforeLoad.

estado.ts exposes parseEstado plus five per-route vocabularies and validateEstado, the one-line validateSearch each of Groups 9–12 will install. The 404's own vocabulary is empty, so _app/$.tsx carries no validateSearch at all — the absence is a declared decision, not an omission.

estado.spec.ts pins each vocabulary with toStrictEqual against the literal R77 table — /login ['error','enviando'], /register ['error'], /invite/$token ['caducada','invalida','ya-miembro'], /profile ['editando','error'], the 404 [] — so the set and its size are both fixed, and a group adding a value without amending R77 goes red. The Implementer's probe adding one value killed 2 tests.

Ten table-driven cases assert no throw and undefined: absent, empty string, misspelled, a value belonging to another route, a repeated parameter (array), numeric, null, an object, and 'constructor' / '__proto__' — the last two because a vocabulary is an array walked with find, which never consults Object.prototype. The Implementer's probe making parseEstado throw outside the vocabulary killed 12 tests.

The vocabularies name states only: no value in any of the five is a width or a breakpoint, and validateEstado reads nothing but search.estado. The 404 itself, this step's only ?estado=-bearing screen, renders both of its explicit arrangements at 390 and at 1230 (measured) with no state parameter involved.

estado.spec.ts filters all five vocabularies for /carga|cargando|loading/ and asserts the result is empty. No Skeleton import exists anywhere in the step's diff. The Implementer's probe adding 'cargando' to ESTADOS_LOGIN killed 2 tests (the R77 set assertion and this one).

No horizontal scroll: documentElement.scrollWidth equals clientWidth at 390 (390/390), 1230x560 and 1230x900. The 44px floor holds on every target measured — the four bar columns are 95.5 x 56, the mobile CTA 350 x 48, the mobile wordmark 123.8 x 44, every rail row 239 x 44, and the desktop CTAs 200 x 44 and 113.1 x 44. The px-1 fix lowered the columns from 97.5 to 95.5, still far above the floor, and the bar's background and hairline still run edge to edge (rect 0..390).

The numerals are

and carry no information; the EmptyState's title holds the real message. Measured after the fix: font-size 88px with line-height 88px and a box of exactly 88px on mobile, 96/96/96 on desktop — the leading-none that cn()/tailwind-merge was eating is now welded to the size as text-[5.5rem]/none and text-[6rem]/none. Negative control (leading-none put back in the base, sizes without the slash, rebuilt): line-height 132px and 144px, boxes 132 and 144 — the previous rejection reproduced exactly. Both brand-mark carry alt="" since the adjacent «memora» word names the link; the two CTAs are text links needing no aria-label.
